title: A revoked device's unused authority authorizes no new effect; completed effects and history stay; a suspected compromise opens a review
problem: On the integration head 8d205324 a DECISION that a delegated device key signed and the body accepted kept its effect after the founder revoked the device: an approved action that had not run yet ran after the revocation, with a grant marked founder-approved. Draft #290 recorded this as an open gap. The founder's policy of 2026-11-11 says revocation must end the device's unused authority at once, keep what was legitimately completed, open a separate review when compromise is suspected, and keep the historical validity of a signature apart from its continuing authority.
baseline: Local branch claude/revoked-device-authority-20261111 on 8d205324 (#196, branch claude/greg-full-machine-completion-whgiee). Not pushed. Reality: unit-tested on real bodies in a container with per-test keys.

alternatives.name: Void in the mission fold at the device.revoked record, write the trail afterwards (chosen)
benefits: no crash window: the rule is derived from one record
holds in every book folded from the ledger, the goal fold included
liabilities: the fold gains three small tables
the trail is a second step that must be finished after a stop (tested)

alternatives.name: Simplest: write decision.withdrawn rows when DEVICE_REVOKE is applied, as a restore does
liabilities: a body that dies between the revocation and the rows keeps the approval for good: the re-sent command is refused because the key is no longer delegated
a device.revoked written by another route (a restore) voids nothing on ended missions

alternatives.name: Strongest competitor: remove voided answers from MissionBook.answers and reopen the same request
benefits: no reader can count a voided answer by mistake
the founder answers the same request
liabilities: the separate appraiser reads that table for history and would refute actions completed before the revocation
every surface and the command path assume one answer per request

alternatives.name: Refuse at the Gate only
liabilities: AuthorityOffice receives scope digests and cannot tell who approved one; it would need the signer threaded through every caller

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: A revoked phone's accepted approvals keep running actions, standing ones for the mission's lifetime.
advantages: no change to the fold or the appraiser
disadvantages: revoking a lost or compromised phone does not stop what it already approved

roles.position: Each sentence of the policy has a tested behaviour: unused authority is voided at the revocation record; completed actions keep their records, receipts and their VERIFIED appraisal; a suspected compromise opens a separate review that changes nothing; the device's signatures still verify as history while its approvals stop authorizing. No protected artifact is touched.
material_concerns: Nine points the sentence does not settle are listed for the founder with the default implemented (ADR, open questions)
The destination is unchanged: a device stays a narrow delegation; this only ends its reach at revocation

roles.position: One rule in the one mission fold (MissionBook._revoked with unused_authority), read by the engine, the goal fold and every surface through tables they already read (withdrawn, consumed). greg/revocation.py owns no authority: it writes what the fold derived and builds the review. No new command kind, store, ledger or authority path.
material_concerns: A voided reconciliation is a new state: no reconciliation ask was ever withdrawn before, so the engine gained two guards (live and ended missions)
The appraiser places a dispatch at its grant's ledger record, not at the mission's later record, so an in-flight dispatch is judged where the Gate claimed it

roles.position: The attacks were written and run by the implementing session itself, one agent. This is not an independent review. Covered by failing-then-passing tests: approve then revoke in one inbox read; a paused body; a decision signed before and delivered after; the same envelope re-sent; the key delegated again; a second device; a forged device.revoked row naming the founder key; a body stopped between the revocation and its trail; a trail written after a new approval of the same scope; an unrecorded reconciliation on a live and on an ended mission; a restore; a device answering the review; a body without the rule judged by the appraiser.
material_concerns: A revocation takes effect at the body's next inbox read; mission steps later in the same turn still run on the approvals as that turn began
Rejections, answer-only records and device-signed resumes are not voided (open questions 1 to 3)
An independent adversarial review has not been done

roles.position: The founder runs `greg device revoke KEY [--suspected-compromise]` and reads `greg device reviews`; `greg status` lists what each revocation voided. A turn pays one fold step and a few lookups; a review is one fold over the ledger prefix, built once. Reverting the branch leaves the written rows as history the old fold already understands.
material_concerns: After a revocation the founder is asked again once per voided decision
A failure while building a review stops a running body, as any turn failure does; the revocation itself is already recorded and in force
The whole test suite was not run here

roles.position: Nothing is deleted or rewritten: voids are appended rows that name the device, the revocation and the answer; the review says what it cannot know. No personal data is added. Claims stay at unit-tested on real bodies in a container; no founder device, no real key, no external effect.
material_concerns: A review lists what a key signed, never who held it
A command the body refused is not attributed to a key

evidence: Reproduction on 8d205324: the phone approves, the founder revokes, both land before the next turn, and the write runs (first test of tests/unit/test_greg_revoked_device_authority.py)
On 8d205324, 17 of the 19 tests of that file that need no new module fail (2 of the 17 only because they read the new MissionBook.voided table); the 2 that pass pin behaviour that already held
On the branch the file passes
scripts/ci/check_revoked_device_mutants.py: every listed safeguard, removed in a scratch copy, fails a test of that file
python -m governance.integrity --check: 13 protected artifacts, all as authorized
python -m acceptance check and python -m acceptance directive --against 8d205324: exit 0
counterevidence: Not run: the whole suite (about 90 minutes), the other mutation gates, the phone page in a browser
This container's known failures on the integration line are unchanged and unrelated (tests/unit/test_greg_native_reconciliation.py fails 9 on the base too: scipy is not installed here)
No independent session or human reviewed the change
A HUMAN_JUDGMENT answer a revoked device signed keeps deciding its question

pass_1.intended_outcome: After a device key is revoked, GREG starts no effect on that key's say-so; everything already done is kept; the founder can ask for one list of everything the key signed.
advantages: the rule cannot be missed by a crash or by another writer of device.revoked
every existing reader of a withdrawal understands a void
history and the appraiser's judgement of completed work are unchanged
disadvantages: the unpaid approve no longer stands for the mission's lifetime when a device signed it and is later revoked
a voided reconciliation needed engine changes
the appraiser gained a second rule to keep in step with the fold
comparisons: against writing rows at command time: no crash window
against removing answers: completed work stays verified
against a Gate-only check: the signer is known in the fold, not at the Gate
rejected_alternatives: removing voided answers from the answers table

pass_2.attack_summary: Re-attacked with pass 1 in place: a trail record landing after the founder approved the same scope again took that scope away (fixed: a void acts at the revocation only; test and mutant); a live mission could close over an interrupted dispatch whose answer was voided when the world already showed the effect (fixed: asked again first; test and mutant); an ended mission recorded a reconciliation in a voided answer's name (fixed; test and mutant); a paused founder was told a voided approval was about to run (fixed in the engine's resolution rule; test and mutant); a dispatch the mission had not recorded when the key was revoked was missing from the review (fixed: the Gate's grant records are read; test and mutant); another device could close a review (fixed: founder key only, on the command path and in the fold; tests and mutants).
new_weaknesses: the appraiser's rule applies to older ledgers too when they are appraised again
the goal's own record of an accepted item stays in the goal registry; the mission-level scope is void and the goal asks again (tested)
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions: the narrowed standing approval: accepted, it is the policy
more asks: accepted, one per voided decision
engine changes for reconciliation: resolved with two guards and tests
two rules to keep in step: bounded by a test that runs a body without the fold rule and requires REFUTED
pass_2.final_design: As in the ADR: the fold voids at the revocation record; revocation.settle writes the trail and the review; the engine asks again; the appraiser refutes a dispatch on a voided approval; the review ask is answered only by the founder key and only recorded.
residual_risks: revocation timing is the next inbox read
rejections, answer-only records and device-signed resumes stand

dissent.handling: Kept as open questions for the founder, each with the default implemented; none is hidden in the code.
entries: Re-pausing what a revoked device resumed would be the more cautious reading of 'unused authority'; this draft does not do it because a resume is a state change already applied, and pausing missions was not asked for
Voiding a revoked device's HUMAN_JUDGMENT answers would be more complete; it needs a compiler change so the question can be asked again

authority_impact.level: narrowing of delegated device authority inside greg/; no constitutional artifact, grant or command kind changes

migration_plan: None required. A ledger that already holds a device.revoked record is folded under the new rule the next time it is read: unused approvals of that key are voided and their trail is written on the next turn. Recorded appraisals are not rewritten.

steps: rows already written stay on the append-only ledger: decision.withdrawn rows with voids_approval are read by the previous fold as a restore's are; device.integrity_review rows and review asks become unread data

kill_criteria: an action is dispatched after a device.revoked record on that key's approval
a revocation changes or removes a recorded answer, action or receipt
an action completed before a revocation is refuted because of it
a review revokes, pauses or rewrites anything, or a device key closes one
a plain DEVICE_REVOKE is recorded or answered differently than before
decision_owner: Alfonso Lopez decides adoption and the nine open questions; the #196 integrator decides intake
review_trigger: Founder review of the draft; an independent adversarial review; intake into #196; the first revocation on a founder-device body
